title: 2023 AMC 10A Problem 23
statement: Positive integer divisors \(a\) and \(b\) of \(N\) are called complementary if \(ab = N.\) Given that \(N\) has a pair of complementary divisors that differ by \(20\) and a pair of complementary divisors that differ by \(23,\) find the sum of the digits of \(N.\)

solutions.text: Complementary divisors differing by \(20\) are \(b\) and \(b + 20\) with product \(N\), so \(N = b^2 + 20b\) and \(N + 100 = (b + 10)^2\). A pair differing by \(23\) gives \(4N + 529 = (2d + 23)^2\). Set \(N + 100 = k^2\). Then \(4k^2 + 129 = m^2\), so \((m - 2k)(m + 2k)\) \(= 129\) \(= 3 \cdot 43\). The positive factor pair \(3,43\) gives \(k=10\), hence the inadmissible value \(N=0\). The pair \(1,129\) gives \(m = 65\), \(k = 32\), hence \(N = 32^2 - 100 = 924\). Check it: \(924 = 22 \cdot 42 = 21 \cdot 44\), and the digit sum is \(9 + 2 + 4 = 15\). Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Complementary divisors with product \(N\) differing by \(20\) are \(b\) and \(b + 20,\) so \(N + 100 = (b + 10)^2\)
Then \(4N + 529\) is also a perfect square; combine the two to get a difference of squares equal to \(129\)
